answer: Recursive Proof Interlocking Toll Agents register by solving a continuous cryptographic puzzle whose difficulty scales with the active peer count in their local cluster. A single agent crossing a meadow computes this alone with minimal latency. However, spinning up sybil nodes forces the attacker to route state updates through a dense vine of interlocking verification checks, rendering hollow nodes computationally impossible to maintain. The attacker pays a direct cost in sustained processing power and memory overhead for every fabricated peer they attempt to inject into the active topology.
